info.name: OpenEMR Clinical Co-Pilot - agent service
info.description:
Runnable collection for the co-pilot agent service.

SETUP (one variable, then press Run):
  baseUrl       already points at the live demo; use http://127.0.0.1:8600 for a local service
  sharedSecret  request it with the demo logins (see the repo README), or your own
                COPILOT_SHARED_SECRET if you are running locally

In the Collection Runner set Delay to 2000 ms: a brief takes 10-30 s and request 4 polls itself.

Every request is HMAC-signed by a collection-level pre-request script, the same scheme the OpenEMR module uses; there is nothing to sign by hand. Run the requests in order: 3 opens a session, 4 polls until the briefs are ready, 5 through 8 exercise one patient, 9 shows the counters and 10 tears down.

The browser never talks to this service in normal use -- OpenEMR proxies every call under the clinician's session -- so this collection is the only way to drive it directly.

Week 2 requests (11-13) read the fixture lab report with the vision model, run the supervisor graph, and render a page with quote boxes. They sit before the close request so the session is still open.

exec: // Signs every request the way the OpenEMR module does, so a grader never has to.
// The service rejects a missing or stale timestamp and any mismatch, so an unsigned
console.warn("Set sharedSecret (collection variable, environment, or newman --env-var). Every signed request returns 401 without it.");
// The signed path is the path only: no host, no query string. Built from the URL segments
// rather than the whole URL, because a pre-request script runs before Postman resolves
// {{variables}} in the address bar -- reading the resolved string here would sign the wrong path.
return value === undefined || value === null ? match : value;
// Substitute variables so the bytes signed are the bytes sent.
var signature = CryptoJS.HmacSHA256(ts + "." + method + "." + path + "." + body, secret).toString(CryptoJS.enc.Hex);

variable.description: Filled in by request 6, used by request 8
Poll counter for request 4; resets itself

request.description: Is the process alive. Checks nothing else on purpose, so a dependency outage never gets a working service killed by an orchestrator. Always 200 while the process runs.

Can the service actually do its job. Probes the model provider, the observability backend and OpenEMR, and checks the provider allowlist and shared secret. Returns 503 when any dependency is unreachable or misconfigured -- it does not return 200 unconditionally. Week 2 adds the vision model that reads documents to the same allowlist check.

exec: pm.test("200 when every dependency is reachable", function () { pm.expect([200,503]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Per-patient readiness. Poll this until every patient reads ready or failed; a brief takes roughly 10-30 s on the free tier, and the whole list has a 90 s budget.

exec: pm.test("every patient has a status", function () { pm.expect(p.length).to.be.above(0); });
// Briefs take 10-30 s each, so this request re-runs itself until they land. That is
// what lets the whole collection work from a single Run instead of needing a human
// to watch it. Bounded, so a stuck brief ends the loop rather than spinning forever.
var settled = p.length > 0 && p.every(function (x) { return x.status === 'ready' || x.status === 'failed'; });

request.description: Makes this patient active and returns their brief. Conversation memory for every other patient is cleared here, so nothing from one chart can reach another's answer. Run step 4 until the patient reads ready, or this returns status=generating with no brief.

A follow-up about the active patient. Every claim in the answer must cite a record a tool returned in this same turn; anything else is deleted before it is returned and listed in removed_claims. Try an out-of-scope pid to see access_denied, or an off-topic question to see the scope statement.

exec: pm.test("every claim carries a citation", function () {

request.description: The patient boundary. A patient who is not the active, authorised one is refused with no content and no hint whether that patient exists, so the reply cannot be used to enumerate.

A clinician rating, attached to the LangSmith trace for that exact answer. Category is a fixed code -- good, mismatch, relevance, completeness, other -- never free text, so a rating can never carry patient data to an external service.

Operational counters since the service started: requests by state, verified and removed claims with the cause of each removal, tool calls, retries, and p50/p95/p99 latency. No identifiers and no clinical content.

Week 2. Reads the fixture two-page lab report with the vision model and returns a LabDocument: every field with a page and quote citation, unsupported fields null with confidence 0. On the free tier this can answer 502 rate_limit; that is the provider's quota, said plainly, not a fault.

exec: pm.test("read, or refused with a named reason", function () { pm.expect([200, 502, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code === 200) { var d = pm.response.json(); console.log("results", d.document.results.length, "unsupported", d.unsupported_fields);

pm.test("every supported value carries a page and quote", function () { d.document.results.forEach(function (r) { if (r.value.value !== null) { pm.expect(r.value.citation.page).to.be.a("number"); pm.expect(r.value.citation.quote).to.be.a("string"); } }); }); }

request.description: Week 2. The supervisor graph for the session's patient with no unread documents: it hands straight to the evidence retriever and returns the brief with the routing. Run after request 3 has opened the session.

exec: pm.test("finished with a brief and logged handoffs", function () { pm.expect(d.phase).to.eql("done"); pm.expect(d.brief).to.be.an("object"); pm.expect(d.handoffs.length).to.be.above(1); d.handoffs.forEach(function (h) { pm.expect(h.reason).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty; }); });

request.description: Week 2. Page 1 of the fixture report as an image, with a box where 'Potassium' is printed. No model: a box is where the text layer says the text is, or found is false.

exec: pm.test("the printed quote is boxed, the absent one is not", function () { pm.expect(d.boxes[0].found).to.eql(true); pm.expect(d.boxes[1].found).to.eql(false); pm.expect(d.image_base64.slice(0, 11)).to.eql("iVBORw0KGgo"); });

request.description: Ends the session and drops every chart and conversation held for it. Sessions also expire after an idle period, and nothing is ever written to disk.
